info.title: Polyhedral surfaces
info.summary: Unit pieces packed on the surface of a convex solid, as small as possible: a Platonic solid (tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron), one of the 13 Archimedean or 13 Catalan solids, a prism, an antiprism or one of the 92 Johnson solids. In fold mode a piece may bend over edges onto the neighbouring faces; in nofold mode each piece stays inside one face.
info.score: the scale s of the solid (its edge length for the Platonic, Archimedean and Johnson solids, prisms and antiprisms); smaller is better

conventions.units: polygon pieces have side 1, disks (N = 0) diameter 1; angles in radians
conventions.solid: solid is a Platonic solid (tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron) of edge s, an Archimedean solid (the same names and unit-edge normalisation as the polyhedra space) of edge s, a Catalan solid (rhombic_dodecahedron, triakis_tetrahedron, deltoidal_icositetrahedron, pentagonal_icositetrahedron, tetrakis_hexahedron, triakis_octahedron, rhombic_triacontahedron, disdyakis_dodecahedron, deltoidal_hexecontahedron, pentagonal_hexecontahedron, pentakis_dodecahedron, triakis_icosahedron, disdyakis_triacontahedron) scaled by s from the polyhedra space's canonical one (the polar reciprocal of the unit-edge Archimedean solid about the midsphere), a prism (prism3, prism5 to prism12) or an antiprism (antiprism4 to antiprism12) of edge s, or a Johnson solid (J1 to J92, the polyhedra space's names such as square_pyramid, gyrobifastigium and triangular_hebesphenorotunda, in its unit-edge normalisation; exact coordinates from python/polyhedra/solids_exact.json after Johnson 1966 and Zalgaller 1967, J44 to J48 in one handedness) of edge s. A face's frame has its origin at the foot of the perpendicular from the solid's centre (for a Johnson solid: at the face's centre, the mean of its vertices) and its last edge (frame vertex M - 1 to frame vertex 0) horizontal at the bottom; a regular face is the regular M-gon of side s centred at the origin, frame vertex k at angle -pi/2 + pi/M + 2 pi k/M. data/surface/solids.json lists the faces and how their edges are glued
conventions.pose: {face, x, y, theta}: the piece centre (x, y) lies in the closed face `face`, in that face's frame; piece vertex k is at angle theta + pi/2 + 2 pi k/N about the centre
conventions.modes: nofold: every piece lies in one closed face; fold: a rigid flat piece is laid out from its centre and continues across edges onto the next faces, no vertex of the solid may lie inside a piece and a piece may not overlap itself
conventions.configuration: {s, pieces: [{face, x, y, theta}, ...]} with P pieces
conventions.score: s, the scale of the solid (the edge for unit-edge solids); smaller is better
conventions.validity: pieces may touch; the server rejects overlaps deeper than 1e-9 (in piece units) with its floating-point validator of the space
conventions.scoring: the score is the size stated in the configuration; the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it
conventions.improvement: an entry is kept only when its score is below the problem's best value (the research record or the site leader, whichever is smaller) by more than a relative 1e-9; one below the research record must also be valid with overlaps of at most 1e-11
conventions.work_limit: the fold check gives up with an error when one piece crosses more than 600 chains of faces (real packings need far fewer); x, y and theta are each at most 10000 in absolute value

info.title: Constant curvature
info.summary: Unit pieces (polygons of side 1, disks of diameter 1) in the smallest regular polygon or disk on a surface of constant curvature K: the hyperbolic plane (K < 0), the flat plane (K = 0) or a sphere of radius 1/sqrt(K) (K > 0). Some problems have no packing at all, because the pieces do not fit in any container.
info.score: the container's side s (polygon) or diameter d (disk) as a geodesic length at curvature K; smaller is better

conventions.space: the complete surface of constant curvature K: hyperbolic plane for K < 0, Euclidean plane for K = 0, sphere of radius 1/sqrt(K) for K > 0
conventions.units: geodesic lengths at curvature K; polygon pieces have side 1, disks (N = 0) diameter 1; angles in radians
conventions.container: centred at the origin O with a horizontal bottom edge: a regular M-gon of geodesic side s, or a disk of diameter d (M = 0); for K > 0 the container lies in the open hemisphere around O
conventions.pose: {x, y, theta}: the centre is the point at geodesic distance sqrt(x^2 + y^2) from O in direction (x, y); theta is the piece's angle relative to the frame carried from O along that geodesic, and a vertex points up at theta = 0; at K = 0 this is PolyPack's usual pose
conventions.configuration: {size, pieces: [{x, y, theta}, ...]} with P pieces; size is s, or d (the diameter) for a disk container
conventions.validity: pieces may touch; the server rejects overlaps deeper than 1e-9 (in piece units) with its floating-point validator of the space; gaps and protrusions are signed geodesic distances
conventions.scoring: the score is the size stated in the configuration; the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it
conventions.improvement: an entry is kept only when its score is below the problem's best value (the research record or the site leader, whichever is smaller) by more than a relative 1e-9; one below the research record must also be valid with overlaps of at most 1e-11
conventions.id: K is written as the catalogue writes it: integers as integers, other values as the shortest decimal that gives the same binary64 number (1e-06, 1.225778283313099)

info.title: Whole sphere
info.summary: Congruent pieces on a whole sphere with no container: the score is the smallest sphere radius that holds them all. For disks this is the Tammes problem.
info.score: the sphere radius rho; smaller is better

conventions.space: the whole sphere of radius rho (curvature 1/rho^2); there is no container
conventions.units: disks (N = 0) of geodesic diameter 1, or regular spherical N-gons of geodesic side 1, on the sphere of radius rho
conventions.pose: {q: [w, x, y, z]}: a quaternion of norm at least 1e-6, each component at most 10000 in absolute value; the piece is the standard piece turned by the rotation of q/|q| (v -> q v q*)
conventions.standard_piece: centred at the north pole (0, 0, 1) of the unit sphere, vertex k at (sin R cos phi_k, sin R sin phi_k, cos R) with phi_k = pi/2 + 2 pi k/N and sin(1/(2 rho)) = sin R sin(pi/N)
conventions.configuration: {rho, pieces: [{q: [w, x, y, z]}, ...]} with P pieces
conventions.validity: pieces may touch; the server rejects overlaps deeper than 1e-9 (in piece units) with its floating-point validator of the space; gaps are measured in length units on the sphere of radius rho
conventions.scoring: the score is the size stated in the configuration; the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it
conventions.improvement: an entry is kept only when its score is below the problem's best value (the research record or the site leader, whichever is smaller) by more than a relative 1e-9; one below the research record must also be valid with overlaps of at most 1e-11

info.title: Flat tori
info.summary: Pieces on a flat torus, a plane that repeats along a lattice: a square or hexagonal torus of side L, or any lattice of the solver's choice. Each piece must also miss its own repeated copies.
info.score: L for the square (sq) and hexagonal (hex) tori, sqrt|det(b1, b2)| for a free lattice; smaller is better

conventions.families: sq: lattice b1 = L (1, 0), b2 = L (0, 1), score L; hex: b1 = L (1, 0), b2 = L (1/2, sqrt(3)/2), score L; free: any basis b1, b2, score sqrt|det(b1, b2)|
conventions.units: polygon pieces have side 1, disks (N = 0) diameter 1; angles in radians
conventions.pose: [x, y, theta] in the plane; positions count modulo the lattice; piece vertex k at (x, y) + R (cos a_k, sin a_k), a_k = theta + pi/2 + 2 pi k/N, R = 1/(2 sin(pi/N))
conventions.configuration: {lattice: {L} for sq and hex or {b1: [x, y], b2: [x, y]} for free, poses: [[x, y, theta], ...]} with P poses
conventions.score: L or sqrt|det(b1, b2)|; smaller is better
conventions.validity: pieces may touch; the server rejects overlaps deeper than 1e-9 (in piece units) with its floating-point validator of the space; the pieces and all their lattice translates must have disjoint interiors, so a piece may not overlap its own translates either
conventions.scoring: the score is the size stated in the configuration; the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it
conventions.improvement: an entry is kept only when its score is below the problem's best value (the research record or the site leader, whichever is smaller) by more than a relative 1e-9; one below the research record must also be valid with overlaps of at most 1e-11
conventions.work_limit: a free basis must be reduced well enough that at most 1000 lattice translates per pair of pieces need checking (a Lagrange-Gauss reduced basis always is); x, y and theta of each pose are each at most 10000 in absolute value
conventions.stored: a kept entry with a free lattice is stored with its basis Lagrange-Gauss reduced and det(b1, b2) > 0: the same lattice and the same score, with the poses as sent

info.title: Polytope boundaries
info.summary: Balls of diameter 1, unit cubes or the other Platonic solids of edge 1 on the boundary of a 4D polytope: the tesseract (balls, axis-aligned cubes, and freely rotated tetrahedra, octahedra, dodecahedra and icosahedra) and, with balls and all five rotated solids (a rotated cube too), the 5-cell, 16-cell, 24-cell, 120-cell and 600-cell, the regular 4-polytopes. The boundary is a closed 3D space made of solid cells (8 cubes for the tesseract) glued face to face. A piece may fold across the faces where two cells meet, but no edge of the polytope may pass through it. The same holds on the d-cubes, d = 5 to 10 (5cube to 10cube, 4D on 5D to 9D on 10D): balls and axis-aligned cubes of dimension d - 1 on the boundary of the d-cube, whose 2d cells are (d-1)-cubes, with no (d-3)-face through a piece. Balls (P = 1 to 24) also fit the boundaries of the d-simplex, d-orthoplex and d-demicube, d = 5 to 10 (5simplex to 10demicube, 18 more containers): their cells are (d-1)-simplices, or (d-1)-simplices and (d-1)-demicubes.
info.score: the edge length s of the polytope; smaller is better

conventions.polytope: polytope is tesseract, 5cell, 16cell, 24cell, 120cell or 600cell: the regular 4-polytope of edge s centred at its vertex centroid (the tesseract is [-s/2, s/2]^4); its boundary is 8 cubes, 5, 16 or 600 tetrahedra, 24 octahedra or 120 dodecahedra (cells), glued face to face; edges and vertices may not lie inside a piece. Around an edge the cells fill 270 (tesseract), 211.6 (5-cell), 282.1 (16-cell), 328.4 (24-cell), 349.7 (120-cell) or 352.6 (600-cell) degrees, short of a full turn. Balls and the tetrahedron, octahedron, dodecahedron and icosahedron (unit edge, freely rotated) fit all six; the cube is axis-aligned on the tesseract and freely rotated on the other five. 5cube to 10cube are the d-cubes [-s/2, s/2]^d, d = 5 to 10: 2d cells that are (d-1)-cubes of edge s, 270 degrees round every (d-3)-face (the hinges, which may not lie inside a piece); balls and axis-aligned cubes fit them. 5simplex to 10simplex, 5orthoplex to 10orthoplex and 5demicube to 10demicube (d = 5 to 10) are the d-simplex (vertices e_i of R^(d+1), d + 1 cells), the d-orthoplex (+-e_i, 2^d cells) and the d-demicube ((+-1/2)^d with an even number of minus signs, 2d + 2^(d-1) cells), of unit edge scaled by s, each centred at its vertex centroid; balls (diameter 1) only, no (d-3)-face through a ball
conventions.cells: cell 2 i + (sigma > 0) is the cube x_i = sigma s/2 of the tesseract, for i = 0..3 and sigma = -1 or +1: cell 0 is x_0 = -s/2, cell 1 is x_0 = +s/2, ..., cell 7 is x_3 = +s/2. The other polytopes' cells are their facets in the engine's order: sorted by outward unit normal, first by the axis of its largest component, then by the sign, then lexicographically (the tesseract's order is a case of it). On the d-cubes cell 2 i + (sigma > 0) is the facet x_i = sigma s/2, i = 0..d-1 (2d cells). On the simplex cell i is the facet opposite vertex e_i (x_i = 0); on the orthoplex cell c is the facet sigma . x = 1 with sigma_i = -1 exactly when bit i of c is set; on the demicube cells 0..2d-1 are the facets x_i = +-s/(2 sqrt 2) (2 i + (sign > 0)) and cell 2d + k the simplex facet at the k-th sign vector w of odd parity, in increasing order of its bit mask
conventions.frame: a point of a cell has local coordinates u = 3 numbers in the cell's frame, its centre at the origin. The frame is the standard basis of R^4 projected on the cell's hyperplane and orthonormalised in order (Gram-Schmidt, skipping the vector nearly parallel to the normal); on the tesseract u = the cell's other three R^4 coordinates in increasing order of index, so the cell is the cube [-s/2, s/2]^3 (in cell 5, x_2 = +s/2, u = (x_0, x_1, x_3)). The polytopes' vertices are listed in docs/spaces/BOUNDARY.md. On the d-cubes u is the cell's other d - 1 coordinates in increasing order, so the cell is [-s/2, s/2]^(d-1). On the simplex, orthoplex and demicube u has d - 1 numbers in the frame of Gram-Schmidt (run twice) on the projections of e_1, e_2, ... onto the cell's tangent space, skipping a vector whose residual is under 1e-9 (docs/spaces/BOUNDARY.md 4D.1), the cell's centre at the origin
conventions.units: balls have diameter 1 (radius 0.5), cubes edge 1 (the cube [-1/2, 1/2]^3 about its centre), the other Platonic solids edge 1 (tetrahedron, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron: docs/spaces/BOUNDARY.md lists their vertices); lengths scale with s, the pieces do not
conventions.pose: {cell, u, q?}: cell is the anchor cell, which holds the piece's centre (0 to 7 on the tesseract, 0 to 4, 15, 23, 119, 599 on the 5-, 16-, 24-, 120- and 600-cell); u = [u0, u1, u2] is the centre in that cell's local coordinates at s and must lie in the closed cell (each component at most 10000 in absolute value); q = [w, x, y, z] is a unit quaternion (norm within 1e-9 of 1) that rotates the standard solid (a Platonic solid of edge 1 centred at the origin, listed in docs/spaces/BOUNDARY.md) in the anchor's frame, absent for no rotation; balls have no q. On the d-cubes (5cube to 10cube) the cell is 0 to 2d - 1, u has d - 1 numbers and there is no q: cubes stay axis-aligned. On the simplex, orthoplex and demicube the cell is 0 to d, 2^d - 1 or 2d + 2^(d-1) - 1, u has d - 1 numbers, balls only and no q
conventions.fold: a piece is laid out from its centre by straight segments that continue across the faces into the next cells, unfolded flat; no point of the edges or vertices may lie inside a piece, and a piece may not overlap itself
conventions.configuration: {s, pieces: [{cell, u, q?}, ...]} with P pieces
conventions.score: s, the edge of the polytope; smaller is better
conventions.validity: pieces may touch; the server rejects overlaps deeper than 1e-9 (in piece units) with its floating-point validator of the space
conventions.scoring: the score is the size stated in the configuration; the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it
conventions.improvement: an entry is kept only when its score is below the problem's best value (the research record or the site leader, whichever is smaller) by more than a relative 1e-9; one below the research record must also be valid with overlaps of at most 1e-11
conventions.nofold: the tesseract's problems also give their nofold value (every piece inside one cell, no folding) and the research record's gain over it, as `extra`
conventions.work_limit: s is at most 10000; the check gives up with a reason when one piece crosses more than 1024 chains of cells (real packings need at most about 80 on the tesseract and 500 on the 120-cell); each component of u and q is at most 10000 in absolute value; checks of balls on the 120-cell from P = 5 and on the 24-cell from P = 22, and of solids from P = 10 on the 120-cell, 13 on the tesseract and 5-cell and 17 on the 16-cell and 24-cell, wait in the heavy queue. The d-cubes take P up to 160 (5cube), 384 (6cube) and 400 (7cube to 10cube), their check gives up with a reason after 4,000,000 search steps (a crowd of balls against the (d-3)-faces; real packings need a few thousand), and checks of 50 ms or more (10cube balls from P = 34) wait in the heavy queue. On the simplex, orthoplex and demicube P is at most 24, the check gives up with a reason after 60,000 search steps or 30,000,000 multiply-adds (60,000,000 on the 8demicube; real packings need at most a few thousand steps), and checks of 50 ms or more (6demicube from P = 3, 7demicube from P = 2, 8demicube always, 10demicube from P = 10) wait in the heavy queue

info.title: Polyhedra
info.summary: 3D in 3D: equal polyhedra (Platonic, Archimedean and Catalan solids, prisms and antiprisms, bipyramids and trapezohedra, and the 92 Johnson solids) packed in the smallest scaled copy of a container polyhedron. The problems and research records are those of polyhedrainpolyhedra.wiki, with PolyPack's improvements, and PolyPack's own problems (prisms and antiprisms with 7, 9, 10 and 11 sides; bipyramids and trapezohedra) with its records. Every ordered pair of the 186 solids is a problem (34,596 pairs, 17,263,404 problems with P from 2 to 500); the 34,446 pairs beyond the 150 named problems have no records yet.
info.score: the scale s of the container solid (its edge length when the container has unit edges); smaller is better

conventions.problems: code is the wiki's <piece>in<container>, e.g. cubintet (cubes in a tetrahedron) or pr3l15incub (triangular prisms of height 1.5 in a cube), or the same for any ordered pair of the 186 solids, the Johnson solids having the codes j01 to j92 (j05inj92: J5 in J92); P from 2 to 500
conventions.solids: the wiki's canonical solids, centred at the origin: unit edges, except the Catalan solids (polar reciprocals of the unit-edge Archimedean solids about the midsphere) and the elongated prisms (base edges 1, lateral edges 1.5, 2 or 3); PolyPack's bipyramids and trapezohedra are likewise the polar reciprocals of the unit-edge prisms and antiprisms about the midsphere. The 92 Johnson solids (Johnson 1966; Zalgaller 1967 for the completeness of the list) are J1 square_pyramid to J92 triangular_hebesphenorotunda, codes j01 to j92, with unit edges, regular faces and the origin at the vertex centroid; J44 to J48 are chiral and only one handedness is stored. Their coordinates are exact algebraic numbers from python/polyhedra/solids_exact.json, which also holds the other solids
conventions.container: s times the canonical container solid, centred at the origin in its canonical orientation
conventions.pose: [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz]: the canonical piece turned by the rotation of q / |q| (v -> q v q*) and centred at (x, y, z); x, y and z at most 10000 and quaternion components at most 1e+100 in absolute value, |q| at least 1e-6
conventions.configuration: {s, pieces: [[x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz], ...]} with P pieces
conventions.validity: pieces may touch; the server rejects overlaps deeper than 1e-9 (in piece units) with its floating-point validator of the space; the overlap of two pieces is their penetration depth, found by the separating-axis test over the face normals of both pieces and the cross products of their edges
conventions.scoring: the score is the size stated in the configuration; the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it
conventions.improvement: an entry is kept only when its score is below the site leader's by more than a relative 1e-9 and below the research record's certified s by more than a relative 1e-6: the records keep the wiki's clearances between pieces and from the walls (up to 1e-7), and removing them is not a better packing; one below the research record must also be valid with overlaps of at most 1e-11

info.title: Balls
info.summary: 3D in 3D: balls of diameter 1 packed in the smallest ball or in the smallest copy of any of the polyhedra space's 186 solids (the classic sphere-packing problems, and balls in a cube, a prism, a Catalan solid), and each of those solids packed in the smallest ball. The problems have no research records yet; the first valid entry of each is kept.
info.score: the container's size s: the diameter of the container ball, or the scale of the container solid (the edge of the cube); smaller is better

conventions.problems: code is <piece>in<container>, 373 of them: ballinball (balls in a ball), ballin<solid> (balls in a solid: ballincub, ballinpkd, ballinpr3, ...) and <solid>inball (a solid in a ball: tetinball, kttinball, pr3l15inball, ...), with <solid> the polyhedra space's code of one of its 186 solids (GET /api/spaces lists all 373); P from 2 to 100
conventions.units: balls have diameter 1 (radius 0.5); the solids are the polyhedra space's canonical solids (edge 1 for the Platonic, Archimedean, prism, antiprism and Johnson solids, 1.5, 2 or 3 for the lateral edges of the elongated prisms, the Catalan, bipyramid and trapezohedron solids their duals), centred at their vertex centroid at the origin
conventions.container: the ball of diameter s about the origin, or s times a canonical solid of the polyhedra space about its vertex centroid (for the cube the cube [-s/2, s/2]^3 of edge s with its faces normal to the axes): the intersection of the half-spaces N_f . x <= s b_f over its faces, N_f the unit outward normal and b_f the offset of face f
conventions.pose: a ball is its centre [x, y, z]; a solid is [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz]: the canonical solid turned by the rotation of q / |q| (v -> q v q*) and centred at (x, y, z); x, y and z at most 10000 and quaternion components at most 1e+100 in absolute value, |q| at least 1e-6
conventions.configuration: {s, pieces: [...]} with P pieces; s positive and at most 1000000
conventions.validity: pieces may touch; the server rejects overlaps deeper than 1e-9 (in piece units) with its floating-point validator of the space; two balls overlap by 2 r minus the distance of their centres, a ball sticks out of a ball by |c| + r - s/2, of a cube by |c_k| + r - s/2 and of another solid by the largest over faces of N_f . c + r - s b_f (r the ball radius); a solid sticks out of the ball by the largest vertex distance minus s/2, and two solids overlap by their penetration depth (the polyhedra space's separating-axis test)
conventions.scoring: the score is the size stated in the configuration; the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it
conventions.improvement: an entry is kept only when its score is below the problem's best value (the research record or the site leader, whichever is smaller) by more than a relative 1e-9; one below the research record must also be valid with overlaps of at most 1e-11

info.title: nD in nD
info.summary: 4D to 10D: equal convex polytopes (the simplex, hypercube and orthoplex of each dimension, the demicube from 5D, the 24-, 120- and 600-cell in 4D, the Gosset polytopes 2_21 and 1_22 in 6D, 3_21 in 7D and 4_21 in 8D) or balls of diameter 1 packed in the smallest scaled copy of a container polytope or ball. The research records are the regular polytopes in 4D to 6D of polyhedrainpolyhedra.wiki's higher-polytope tab, re-certified; every other problem has none yet and takes its first valid entry.
info.score: the container's size s: the scale of the container polytope (its edge when the container has unit edges), or the diameter of the container ball; smaller is better

conventions.problems: d from 4 to 10; piece and container are a polytope of that dimension (simplex, cube, ortho, demi from 5D, 24cell, 120cell and 600cell in 4D, 221 and 122 in 6D, 321 in 7D, 421 in 8D) or ball, any ordered pair, e.g. ndim/4/cube/ortho/12 (hypercubes in an orthoplex) or ndim/6/ball/221/9; P from 2 to 40 in 4D, 32 in 5D, 24 in 6D and 20 from 7D (GET /api/spaces lists the ranges)
conventions.units: polytopes have unit edges and are centred at their vertex centroid; balls have diameter 1 (radius 0.5); the catalogue is docs/spaces/NDIM.md section 2 (the generator proves each polytope in exact arithmetic)
conventions.container: s times the catalogue polytope about the origin (the intersection of the half-spaces N_f . x <= s b_f, N_f the unit outward normal and b_f the offset of facet f), or the ball of diameter s about the origin
conventions.pose: a polytope piece is [t_1..t_d, k_1..k_m, flip] with m = d(d-1)/2 and the flip optional (0 when absent): the canonical piece turned by R = D (I - S)^-1 (I + S), S the skew matrix with S[i][j] = k (i < j, row by row) and D the diagonal matrix with -1 at the set bits of the flip (an even number of them), then centred at t; centre coordinates at most 10000, each k at most 32 in absolute value; a ball is its centre [t_1..t_d]
conventions.configuration: {s, pieces: [pose, ...]} with P poses; s positive and at most 1e6
conventions.validity: pieces may touch; the server rejects overlaps deeper than 1e-9 (in piece units) with its floating-point validator of the space; two pieces overlap by their penetration depth (GJK and EPA on the Minkowski difference), a polytope sticks out by the largest N_f . x - s b_f over its vertices and facets, a ball piece by N_f . c + 0.5 - s b_f, and a ball container by the farthest point's distance minus s/2
conventions.scoring: the score is the size stated in the configuration; the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it
conventions.improvement: an entry is kept only when its score is below the site leader's by more than a relative 1e-9 and below the research record's s by more than a relative 1e-6: the records keep the wiki's clearance of 1e-7 between pieces and from the walls, and removing it is not a better packing; an entry of a problem without a record, or one below the record, must also be valid with overlaps of at most 1e-11
conventions.work_limit: a check is stopped, with a reason, after 8 s of processor time; checks of large containers (the 4_21 polytope has 19,440 facets) or many pieces share the server's queue of heavy checks, one at a time, and are refused with 503 when it is full

exhibits.name: sweep
exhibits.title: Curvature sweeps
exhibits.summary: How the best packings change as the curvature K changes slowly. The best size never jumps, but it has corners, and the arrangement of the pieces can jump where two arrangements are equally good.
